We’ll go from a simple comedy idea to a full 4-scene animated story using original characters, visual gags, exaggerated reactions, chaotic situations, and fast punchlines designed to keep the story moving.

The workflow is simple: ChatGPT generates the concepts and scene prompts, Google Flow turns those prompts into images and animations, and CapCut brings everything together into the final video.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━


⏰ Timestamps

00:00 Intro & Channel Analysis
00:42 Finding the 2D Comedy Format

03:28 Scene Continuation & Final Edit


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━


🎬 In This Video You’ll Learn:

• How to create original 2D comedy concepts with ChatGPT
• How to turn one idea into a complete 4-scene story
• How to generate image and video prompts automatically
• How to create consistent scenes using previous frames
• How to animate 2D cartoon characters with Google Flow
• How to use Nano Banana 2 for scene generation
• How to use Veo for AI animation
• How to create visual gags and exaggerated cartoon reactions
• How to continue an animation from the previous scene
• How to combine multiple AI-generated clips in CapCut
• How to build fast-paced visual comedy without traditional animation software


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━


🛠 AI Tools Used

• ChatGPT
• Google Flow
• Nano Banana 2
• Veo
• CapCut


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━


🚀 The Workflow

The process starts with ChatGPT generating multiple original comedy concepts. From there, we choose one idea and let the master prompt turn it into a complete scene-by-scene blueprint.

Then we create the first image in Google Flow, animate it, save the final frame, and use that frame to continue the next scene. This keeps the characters, environment, and story connected instead of rebuilding everything from scratch.

Finally, all the clips go into CapCut where we tighten the pacing, remove slow moments, and line up the reactions and punchlines.

The result is a complete 2D comedy sequence built from a simple idea and a repeatable AI workflow.

You can swap the raccoon for a dog, mouse, penguin, human, or completely original character. Change the location, the problem, the visual gag, or the final punchline, and you can build a totally different story using the same workflow.
